claims.claim_vi: Imperative programming changes program state through a sequence of commands, uses control structures like loops and conditionals, emphasizes mutable data and explicit steps; examples C, Python and most procedural languages.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Functional programming relies on pure functions without side effects, promotes immutability, supports higher-order functions, recursion and declarative programming; examples Haskell, Lisp, Scala and functional features in JavaScript.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Object-oriented programming models real-world entities as objects with data and methods, encourages inheritance, encapsulation and polymorphism, uses classes, objects and interfaces; examples Java, C++, Python, Ruby.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Python functional HOWTO: procedural, declarative, object-oriented and functional approaches; objects have internal state and methods; Smalltalk and Java are object-oriented while C++ and Python support but do not force it; in functional programming functions ideally only take inputs and produce outputs and functions without side effects are called purely functional; a higher-order function takes functions as input or returns a function; Lisp, C++ and Python are multi-paradigm.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: The source gives no comparison of merit, no code and no guidance on choosing a paradigm; the language lists are examples only.
